title: The Alert guard at the gate
subtitle: 责任担当 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 责任担当（做人与做事·责任与担当）
meta: 主题语境：责任担当（做人与做事·责任与担当）　|　核心词汇：alert　|　正文 334 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 alert 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1956 the craftsman wrote of ① an alert guard at the gate in the ledger, and everybody in the workshop said at once that it was ② more alert than the one named there the year before. Three years on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the craftsman, who never explained anything, had done it without a word of thanks and gone home; it was the alert ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the most alert guard at the gate anybody in the workshop had ever seen, or so the ledger for August 1950 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too alert to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the apprentice who had come to help; the alert ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the tool at the far bench, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ an alert mind, and said that no apprentice in his right mind would call it ⑥ as alert as the mind they had once had in the old workshop. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was alert or not, and he said so.

By 1963 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the ledger. What the line asked for was ⑦ something alert, and nothing besides. The apprentice from the next workshop called the whole plan ⑧ quite alert; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the ledger kept the names of the alert ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1966, at once, she wrote of another alert guard at the gate in the same ledger, and the work, which took two years, seemed ⑨ more alert than anybody had expected. ⑩ The most alert mind in the whole workshop, she said in 1968, was the one she could never quite name; the alert ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 警觉（前置定语 an alert guard at the gate：1956 年匠人在工料簿里记下的那件警觉的守卫）
B. adj. 警觉／机敏（比较级 more alert than：文中两处，一处比门边的守卫，一处比预想）
C. adj. 警觉／机敏（最高级 the most alert：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 警觉（表语 too alert to do：母亲觉得它太警觉，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 机敏（前置定语 an alert mind：叔叔把整件事称作一桩机敏的头脑）
F. adj. 机敏（同级比较 as alert as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩头脑相比）
G. adj. 机敏（后置定语 something alert：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 机敏（受程度副词修饰 quite alert：那位学徒的评价）

items.q: an alert guard at the gate
the most alert guard at the gate anybody

answers.why: alert 意为“警觉”，1956 年匠人在工料簿里记下的是“一件警觉的守卫”，此处作前置定语 an alert guard at the gate。
alert 意为“警觉”，此处用比较级 more alert than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
alert 意为“警觉”，工料簿上 八月 那行字说它是工坊里最警觉的一件，故用最高级 the most alert guard at the gate。
alert 意为“警觉”，母亲认为这件东西“太警觉了，谁也用不上”，too alert to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
alert 意为“机敏”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩机敏的头脑”，此处作前置定语 an alert mind。
alert 意为“机敏”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩头脑一样机敏”，同级比较用 as alert as。
alert 意为“机敏”，工料簿上那半行字要的是“机敏的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something alert。
alert 意为“机敏”，邻工坊来的那位学徒认为这套计划“相当机敏”，quite 修饰原级 alert。
alert 意为“机敏”，1966 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要机敏”，故用比较级 more alert than。
alert 意为“机敏”，母亲 1968 年说的是“整个工坊里最机敏的那一桩”，故用最高级 the most alert mind。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1956 年，匠人在工料簿里记下了一件警觉的守卫。（an alert guard at the gate）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更警觉。（more alert than …）
母亲觉得它太警觉，谁也用不上。（too alert to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩机敏的头脑。（an alert mind）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩头脑一样机敏。（as alert as …）
到了 1963 年，工料簿上只剩半行字：要的是一件机敏的东西。（something alert）
answers: In 1956 the craftsman wrote of an alert guard at the gate in the ledger.
Everybody said it was more alert than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too alert to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business an alert mind.
He said nobody would call it as alert as the mind they had once had.
By 1963 the ledger asked for nothing but something alert.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 alert 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1956 the craftsman wrote of an alert guard at the gate in the ledger, and nobody forgot it.
It was the most alert guard at the gate in the workshop, or so the ledger says.
My mother thought it too alert to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business an alert mind, and nobody argued with him.
The apprentice from the next workshop called the plan quite alert, and everybody laughed.
The alert ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
